qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global platform breadth and embedded multi-facility outsourcing relationships create switching costs for large corporate enterprise accounts. However, fails proof of moat: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~8% (below the 12% hurdle rate) with structural operating margins of only 4-6%. Primary erosion threats include severe cyclicality in transaction advisory, competitive fee compression across multi-vendor facilities management RFPs (competing against JLL, Cushman & Wakefield, Colliers), and broker talent mobility.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & lack of pricing power, REJECT). While CBRE is the leading global commercial real estate services platform with an asset-light footprint and sticky enterprise facilities contracts, its economic engine generates structurally thin operating margins (~4-6%) and sub-hurdle capital returns (5-year median GAAP ROIC ~8% vs. 12% threshold). Highly cyclical transaction advisory and procurement-driven pricing pressure in outsourcing prevent demonstrated pricing power above inflation across the cycle.
qualitative.evidence: Historical GAAP ROIC has averaged 7.5%-8.5% over the last 5 years (2020: ~9.5%, 2021: ~10.5%, 2022: ~9.5%, 2023: ~6.7%, 2024: ~7.5%, 2025: ~8.5%-9.5%), failing the 12% minimum threshold across the cycle. Operating margins are structurally low at 4.0%-6.5%, and net margins sit at 2.0%-4.0%, diluted by pass-through client-reimbursed costs in Building Operations & Experience (BOE) and heavy commission splits in Advisory Services. While revenue expanded from ~$35.8B in 2023 to ~$40.5B in 2024 and ~$41.0B in 2025 led by corporate outsourcing resilience, transaction and capital markets earnings remain highly volatile and price-taker in nature during commercial real estate contractions.
